title: Bulgogi
subtitle: Grilled marinated beef with pear and soy sauce
excerpt: Bulgogi is thinly sliced beef marinated in soy sauce, Asian pear, garlic, and sesame oil, then cooked quickly on a hot griddle or in a pan. The pear tenderises the meat and adds a gentle sweetness that balances the salty marinade.
sourceNotes: Bulgogi, meaning 'fire meat', has roots in the Goguryeo kingdom over 1,600 years ago. It was historically cooked over an open flame on a perforated grill pan. Today it appears on restaurant menus and home tables across Korea and is one of the most widely recognised Korean dishes internationally.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the raw marinated beef for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and cook straight from cold.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the marinade and beef. Cook in batches so the pan stays hot and the meat chars rather than steams.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate overnight in the fridge for deeper flavour.

glossaryTerms.definition: A dark, fragrant oil pressed from toasted sesame seeds. It is used as a finishing oil in Korean cooking rather than for frying, as its flavour is strong and its smoke point is low.

content.text: Bulgogi takes 25 minutes of active work and serves 4, but the beef needs at least 1 hour in the marinade. The name means 'fire meat' and the dish is built around that quick, high-heat cook. Thin slices of beef pick up the marinade fast and cook in just a few minutes.

Slice the beef as thinly as you can. If you put it in the freezer for 20 minutes first it becomes firm enough to slice easily. Asian pear in the marinade acts as a natural tenderiser. If you cannot find Asian pear, a small ripe regular pear will work, but use slightly less as the flavour is stronger. Finish the cooked beef with a few drops of
Combine the soy sauce, sesame oil, mirin, sugar, garlic, and ginger in a bowl. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the beef slices and spring onions to the marinade. Mix well so every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Heat a griddle pan or heavy frying pan over a very high heat until smoking. Add the marinated beef in a single layer. Do not overcrowd the pan or the meat will steam rather than char.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until the beef is caramelised and cooked through. Work in batches if needed, wiping the pan between batches.
Transfer to a plate. Scatter sesame seeds over the top. Serve with steamed short-grain rice and any extra spring onions.

items.cause: The slices were too thick or the pan was not hot enough
items.fix: Slice as thin as possible, ideally 3mm or less. Make sure the pan is very hot before adding the beef so it sears quickly.

items.cause: Sugar in the marinade scorches over very high heat
items.fix: Shake off excess marinade before adding beef to the pan. Cook in small batches so the pan temperature stays high and the meat cooks through before the sugar burns.

items.cause: Too much beef in the pan at once, creating steam
items.fix: Cook in smaller batches. Each piece needs direct contact with the hot pan surface.

content.text: Bulgogi is a Korean classic. It is eaten at home and in restaurants. It is often wrapped in lettuce leaves. It goes with rice and pickled kimchi. It is one of the first Korean dishes many people try. It suits weeknight cooking well.
